issues.item: Photographic Recall: Remembering what happened during the frightening event is just like looking at photographs of it in my mind.
issues.explanation: Within the Memory node, 'photographic recall' implies a vivid, picture-like recollection of the trauma, while 'the memory feels like it belongs to someone else' suggests marked depersonalization/detachment from the memory. These can occasionally coexist, but paired with 'parts of the event I cannot remember no matter how hard I try,' the memory profile becomes internally strained: simultaneously highly vivid, markedly inaccessible, and experienced as not one's own. For this specific MVC profile, that combination is hard to interpret as a coherent single memory presentation rather than an overmixed set of memory phenomena.

For a life-threatening motor vehicle collision, triggers involving 'related people' and a 'related voice' are hard to reconcile unless the crash specifically involved identifiable individuals whose voices became trauma cues. Given the rest of the profile centers on generic crash-related danger (similar cars, world is dangerous, hypervigilance), these interpersonal/voice triggers are the least coherent trauma-linked items.

'I have no future' is possible in severe PTSD, but in this profile it is less well integrated with the otherwise fear-based collision formulation, which emphasizes danger, vigilance, and fragmented trauma memory rather than pervasive foreshortened future or depressive-collapse themes. It is not impossible, but it is the most weakly connected appraisal item here.
